3	## Overview
4	This collection of four datasets tracks the economic transformation of the global energy sector from 2010 to 2024. It covers the declining levelized cost of energy for solar PV, onshore wind, and battery storage; the cost range of new fossil fuel generation; cumulative renewable installed capacity; and annual global fossil fuel subsidies.
5	
6	## Data Source
7	
8	### lcoe_trends
9	Annual LCOE values for three technologies: `solar_pv`, `onshore_wind`, and `battery_storage`. All values in 2023 real USD per MWh. 15 rows (2010–2024). Solar PV ranges from 359 to 33; onshore wind from 95 to 35; battery storage from 1,100 to 102.
10	
11	### fossil_fuel_lcoe_range
12	Biennial LCOE ranges for new-build gas CCGT (`gas_ccgt_low`, `gas_ccgt_high`) and coal (`coal_low`, `coal_high`). 8 rows at even-year intervals. Values in 2023 real USD/MWh. These define the reference band against which renewable crossover points are identified.
13	
14	### installed_capacity
15	Cumulative global installed capacity in GW for `solar_pv_gw` and `onshore_wind_gw`. 15 rows (2010–2024). Solar PV grows from 40 to 1,950 GW; onshore wind from 178 to 960 GW.
16	
17	### fossil_fuel_subsidies
18	Annual global fossil fuel subsidies in nominal billion USD, split into `consumption_subsidies_bn` and `production_subsidies_bn`, with a `total_subsidies_bn` sum. 15 rows (2010–2024). Total ranges from ~290 to ~700 billion.
19	
20	## Data Notes
21	- LCOE figures are illustrative estimates aligned with IRENA and BloombergNEF reporting trends but rounded for clarity.
22	- Battery storage LCOE reflects 4-hour lithium-ion systems.
23	- 2022 spike in fossil LCOE and subsidies reflects the global energy price crisis.
24	- Fossil fuel subsidy estimates cover direct government subsidies only; implicit subsidies (e.g., unpriced externalities) are excluded.
25	- 2024 values are preliminary estimates.

Levelized costs of solar PV, onshore wind, and battery storage have collapsed 89–91% since 2010 — crossing below new-build fossil fuel ranges while installed capacity scaled exponentially and annual fossil fuel subsidies remained persistently high.

Consumption Subsidies ($B)
Production Subsidies ($B)
Battery Storage · USD/MWh (2023 real)
Battery Cost Collapse: –91% in 14 Years
From $1,100/MWh in 2010 to $102/MWh in 2024 — the steepest proportional decline of all tracked technologies alongside solar PV.
Solar Crossover: ~2017
Solar PV LCOE ($72/MWh) crossed below the gas CCGT upper range (~$52–$78/MWh) around 2017 and definitively below the gas floor by 2019. By 2024, solar at $33/MWh is less than half the cheapest new-build gas plant.
Wind Crossover: ~2016
Onshore wind reached parity with the cheapest new-build gas around 2016 at $56/MWh. By 2020 it matched the coal floor ($65/MWh). Today at $35/MWh wind is the cheapest utility-scale electricity source in most markets.
Subsidy Divergence
Even as renewables became the cheapest power option, global fossil fuel subsidies reached a record $700B in 2022 (energy price crisis spike) and remain at $550B in 2024 — 34% above 2010 levels. The divergence between clean energy economics and incumbent spending is widening.

Data: IRENA, BloombergNEF, IEA — 2023 real USD/MWh for LCOE; nominal USD for subsidies. Battery storage reflects 4-hour lithium-ion systems. Fossil fuel subsidy estimates cover direct government subsidies only. 2024 values are preliminary estimates.
